Most favorable hourly samples

    Windows use only astronomical darkness (Sun below −18°) within the selected 24/48/72-hour forecast. Consecutive Fair/Good timestamps are ranked by mean suitability. These are hourly samples, not verified continuous clear periods. Times use the location’s timezone and the selected 24/48/72-hour range.

    Suitability rules and data confidence

    CMC indices: 0 = cloudy, 1 = very poor, 2 = poor, 3 = average/medium, 4 = good, 5 = excellent. Higher is better. Zero is not missing. Preferred ranges are soft preferences, not cutoffs. Every rating requires valid seeing, transparency, cloud cover, wind, humidity, air temperature, dew point, Sun altitude, Moon altitude and illumination. Missing or invalid inputs give null / Insufficient data; complete coverage does not imply forecast certainty.

    Separate category-specific seeing and transparency curves form atmospheric suitability. Seeing/transparency weights: wide-field 25/75%, broadband and narrowband 20/80%, planetary and lunar 85/15%. Cloud, wind, dew-risk, twilight and moonlight modifiers can only reduce that result; there is no favorable baseline for poor indices. Seeing has the greatest influence on planetary and lunar detail; transparency has a stronger influence on broadband. Narrowband is more tolerant of moonlight, but not clouds or haze. Poor <40, Marginal 40–54, Fair 55–69, Good ≥70. These are uncalibrated planning choices.

    ✳ nightwatch.

    Made for the moments between sunset and sunrise.

    Weather: Open-Meteo · Astronomy: SunCalc · Seeing/transparency: ECCC/CMC

    Forecast data and missing values

    Weather forecasts come from Open-Meteo: cloud cover, relative humidity, temperature, dew point, wind speed, and precipitation probability. Forecasts are model outputs, not measurements at your telescope.

    Seeing and transparency are provider-issued CMC/ECCC RDPS indices from MSC GeoMet, loaded for the selected location and exact UTC forecast hour. They are not arcseconds or measurements at your telescope. The model grid is about 10 km and covers North America. Provider condition labels, valid time, and model run are displayed. No temporal interpolation, extrapolation, or derived conversion is used. Missing or invalid values remain null. The viewing score is inferred by Nightwatch, not supplied by CMC or Open-Meteo. For each hour, cloud component = 100 − cloud%; humidity component = 100 − max(0, RH% − 40) × 1.4; wind component = max(0, 100 − 3 × wind in km/h); moon component = 100 − illuminated percent when the Moon is above the horizon, otherwise 100. These receive weights 60%, 15%, 10%, and 15%. The total is clamped to 0–100, multiplied by 1 below −18° Sun altitude, 0.65 from −18° to below −12°, or 0.25 during the remaining twilight, then rounded. Daylight is zero. Any missing required input returns null. Viewing colors use green for “Good” ≥70, yellow for “Fair” 55–69, orange for “Marginal” 40–54, and red for “Poor” below 40. Unavailable scores stay gray. These thresholds are uncalibrated planning choices. CMC seeing and transparency and light pollution do not enter this formula. Location-specific Bortle and sky-brightness values can be supplied by DarkSkySites through a server-side proxy. These are provider model outputs and a provider-derived Bortle class, not measurements. Dataset date, fallback and quality are shown. Values with unscreened quality, including unverified-zero data, remain null. Any known local readings you saved override the corresponding provider value and are labeled user supplied. This app does not convert between SQM and Bortle. If the backend is not configured or data is unavailable, automatic values stay null. Missing weather values also remain null, with no interpolation or substitution.

    Sun and Moon geometry and illumination are calculated with SunCalc. Darkness means the Sun is below −18°. Twilight crossings are calculated to one-minute resolution, not supplied as measured data.

    Dew guidance is a rule, not a dew prediction: use a heater when relative humidity is at least 85% or the air/dew-point spread is at most 3°C (5.4°F). Otherwise a heater is not indicated by those thresholds; keep it available. Missing any required input makes the recommendation null. No optical surface temperature is available.

    The maps use OpenStreetMap for geography and ECCC GeoMet for GOES infrared satellite imagery and CMC RDPS total cloud cover, 10m wind speed, and 2m air temperature. Wind and temperature map legend labels convert the provider’s native values to the selected unit system while preserving its color gradient and forecast values. The map distance scale follows that unit choice. Imperial is the default unless a metric preference was saved. Dew/frost badges are disclosed inferred equipment-risk indicators: humidity ≥85% or temperature/dew-point spread ≤3°C (5.4°F), with frost possible at air temperatures ≤3°C (37.4°F) and dew possible otherwise. This is a conservative screen, not a provider-issued condensation forecast or a surface-temperature measurement. No badge is rendered when the screen is negative or a required input is missing; absent badges do not establish safe or dry optics. NOAA SWPC supplies the short-term OVATION aurora grid with its observation and forecast times; it is not extended to the chart’s 24/48/72-hour horizon. Nightwatch shows the supplied 0–100 aurora values, not a personal visibility probability. Local values are taken from the nearest 1° NOAA grid cell without interpolating missing values. Satellite timestamps come from provider metadata and are not real-time measurements at the marker. CMC images use the selected exact forecast hour and pinned model run without time interpolation. Imagery may be blank outside coverage; a blank image does not establish clear conditions. The recent-image animation uses six provider timestamps, not generated intermediate frames. The 24/48/72-hour tabs start now. Each row represents the upcoming hourly forecast timestamp, displayed in the location’s time zone. Links to observing guides do not imply a verified event or visibility forecast.
